new_entities.name: Spironolactone for resistant hypertension
aliases: spironolactone add-on therapy for resistant hypertension
mineralocorticoid receptor blockade in resistant hypertension
new_entities.description: Use of spironolactone as add-on treatment for resistant hypertension already treated with multiple standard antihypertensive agents.

new_entities.name: Blood pressure outcomes
aliases: home or clinic systolic blood pressure control
new_entities.description: Measured blood-pressure outcomes such as home systolic blood pressure lowering or improved blood pressure control.

edges.effect_quant: PATHWAY-2 showed spironolactone lowered home systolic blood pressure 8.70 mm Hg more than placebo and about 4 mm Hg more than either bisoprolol or doxazosin. Earlier meta-analysis found aldosterone antagonists reduced systolic blood pressure by 16.5 mm Hg versus control across resistant-hypertension studies, and PATHWAY-2 mechanistic analyses reinforced that sodium-retention physiology predicts a strong spironolactone response.
edges.population: adults with resistant hypertension despite treatment with maximally tolerated multidrug regimens
edges.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid receptor blockade counteracts aldosterone-driven sodium retention and volume expansion, which appears to be a dominant mechanism in many patients with resistant hypertension.
edges.summary: This is one of the best supported add-on drug edges in hypertension. Spironolactone is not just another option in resistant hypertension; it has repeatedly outperformed the obvious comparators.
edges.caveats: Hyperkalemia risk still matters, especially in CKD or when combined with renin-angiotensin system blockade. The benefit is best established in carefully characterized resistant hypertension rather than casual intensification of simpler hypertension regimens.

evidence.notes: Spironolactone versus placebo, bisoprolol, and doxazosin to determine the optimal treatment for drug-resistant hypertension. PATHWAY-2.
